top_examples.hook: My coworker stole my lunch for an entire week, then reported me to HR because the last one was too spicy.
top_examples.premise: A coworker secretly steals the narrator's homemade lunches for a week, then reports the narrator to HR after taking a naturally extra-spicy meal.
top_examples.title: She Stole My Lunch, Then Reported Me to HR

top_examples.hook: My neighbor filed three noise complaints about my dog. I don't own a dog.
top_examples.premise: A woman receives repeated condo noise complaints about a dog she does not own, then discovers her neighbor has been playing barking sounds outside her door to manufacture evidence and pressure her to move.
top_examples.title: She Reported My Dog. I Don't Own One.

top_examples.hook: I found a jewelry receipt in my boyfriend's jacket, and for three days I was absolutely sure he was about to propose.
top_examples.premise: A woman thinks her boyfriend is secretly planning to propose after finding a hidden jewelry receipt, but discovers he bought an expensive bracelet for his mother to replace one he accidentally lost years ago.
top_examples.title: I Thought He Was About to Propose

top_examples.hook: My manager stole my entire presentation, but he forgot to check the last slide.
top_examples.premise: A woman spends weeks building a client presentation, only for her manager to remove her name and present it as his own, until the client asks about a hidden appendix slide he never bothered to read.
top_examples.title: My Manager Stole My Presentation—Then the Client Opened the Last Slide

top_examples.hook: My roommate charged us a fake building fee for six months—then the landlord knocked on our door asking why the rent was late.
top_examples.premise: A woman discovers that the roommate who handles the apartment bills has been collecting a fake monthly maintenance fee from everyone while repeatedly paying the real rent late.
top_examples.title: My Roommate Invented a Fake Rent Fee

recent_story_cards.conflict: Angry customers arrive demanding missing cakes while the narrator insists she never accepted their orders and cannot understand why they have her building address.
recent_story_cards.payoff: My neighbor didn't steal my recipes. She stole my reputation and used my lobby as customer service.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman keeps receiving one-star reviews for a home bakery order page she barely uses, then discovers a neighbor has copied her photos and address to run a fake pickup bakery from her apartment lobby.
recent_story_cards.title: My Neighbor Opened a Fake Bakery Using My Address
recent_story_cards.twist: A customer shows her the fake bakery page, where the neighbor copied old cake photos and listed the narrator's lobby as the pickup point to avoid revealing her own identity.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The roommate blames cheap batteries and denies anyone enters while the narrator is at work, even though toiletries keep moving and towels disappear.
recent_story_cards.payoff: The lock wasn't malfunctioning. My bathroom had business hours.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman thinks her apartment's smart lock is malfunctioning because the battery drains constantly, then discovers her roommate has been giving temporary access codes to strangers to use their shower after nearby gym classes.
recent_story_cards.title: Strangers Kept Using Our Shower While I Was at Work
recent_story_cards.twist: The lock's access history shows dozens of short daytime entries using guest codes named after days of the week, and a stranger arrives holding a towel and asking whether the shower is free.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The friend controls every group photo and repeatedly delays sharing the originals while insisting she is still editing them.
recent_story_cards.payoff: We thought she was documenting our vacation. She thought we were funding her photo shoot.
recent_story_cards.premise: A couple's friend keeps volunteering to photograph their group trips for free, then they discover she has been cropping everyone out and licensing the vacation photos to a travel page as solo-content shoots.
recent_story_cards.title: Our Group Vacation Became Her Sponsored Content
recent_story_cards.twist: One friend sees their rented villa, picnic setup, and even his birthday cake in a sponsored travel post where the photographer presents the trip as her own curated getaway.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Parents keep contributing small amounts because each request sounds plausible, while nobody wants to look stingy in the group chat.
recent_story_cards.payoff: He wasn't organizing team gifts. He was charging us a politeness tax.
recent_story_cards.premise: A father discovers another parent at his son's sports club has been collecting cash for a nonexistent team gift by repeatedly changing the supposed recipient.
recent_story_cards.title: The Team Gift Fund Had No Gifts
recent_story_cards.twist: At the season-ending party, three different coaches thank the parents for gifts they never received, and screenshots reveal the organizer used the same payment link each time.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The seller repeatedly claims the bank reversed part of the payment and pressures the buyer to return the ring temporarily while refusing to provide clear transaction records.
recent_story_cards.payoff: He wasn't selling engagement rings. He was running proposals on a revolving door.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man buys a supposedly unused engagement ring from a local seller, then learns the seller has been renting the same ring to multiple people for proposal photos before demanding it back over invented payment problems.
recent_story_cards.title: The Seller Tried to Repossess My Engagement Ring
recent_story_cards.twist: A jeweler recognizes the ring's unusual engraving and reveals another customer brought in the exact same ring after a proposal only weeks earlier.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Residents receive repeated warning notices despite carefully sorting their recycling, while the volunteer insists contamination proves people are careless.
recent_story_cards.payoff: He wasn't cleaning up our recycling. He was editing it for profit.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man discovers his building's enthusiastic recycling volunteer has been removing refundable cans from residents' bags, then reporting those same residents for improper sorting to keep control of the recycling room.
recent_story_cards.title: Our Recycling Monitor Was Planting the Trash
recent_story_cards.twist: A hallway camera shows the volunteer opening sorted bags, taking refundable containers, and moving rejected trash into them before photographing the evidence.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The organizer keeps adding premium dishes and drinks while assuring everyone the costs are handled, leaving the birthday guest unaware of any payment expectation.
recent_story_cards.payoff: He didn't throw me a birthday dinner. He made a reservation in my wallet's name.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man's friend offers to organize a surprise birthday dinner, then secretly upgrades everything and tells the restaurant the birthday guest will cover the entire bill.
recent_story_cards.title: My Surprise Birthday Came With the Entire Bill
recent_story_cards.twist: When the bill arrives, the server hands it directly to the birthday guest because the organizer had explicitly listed him as the host and cardholder when making the reservation.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The manager publicly presents the proposal as his initiative while privately telling the narrator that anonymous suggestions belong to the company, not the person who submitted them.
recent_story_cards.payoff: He took credit for my idea and forgot to remove my name from the evidence.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man's manager praises an anonymous employee suggestion that saves the department money, then claims it as his own idea after learning it came from the narrator.
recent_story_cards.title: My Manager Stole an Anonymous Suggestion
recent_story_cards.twist: During an executive presentation, the manager cannot answer a technical question and opens the original suggestion attachment, which still contains the narrator's name in the document metadata and revision comments.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The boyfriend dismisses each reservation as a canceled work booking while points disappear from the narrator's account and staff greet him like a regular.
recent_story_cards.payoff: I thought he was secretly planning romance. He was secretly farming loyalty points.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman thinks her boyfriend is secretly planning romantic surprises because restaurant confirmations keep appearing on their shared tablet, but discovers he is using her loyalty account to take clients out and collect rewards personally.
recent_story_cards.title: I Thought the Secret Reservations Were for Me
recent_story_cards.twist: At a restaurant she visits with friends, the host thanks her for being such a loyal customer and mentions the boyfriend's recurring corporate dinners booked under her membership.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Unexpected strangers keep arriving with luggage and claiming the cousin said they could stay, while the narrator is responsible for the cat and has nowhere else to sleep.
recent_story_cards.payoff: The cat wasn't the anxious one. My cousin was anxious about paying for either a sitter or a hotel for her friends.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman agrees to pet-sit her cousin's supposedly anxious cat for a weekend, then discovers the cousin has promised the same apartment to visiting friends as free accommodation without telling her.
recent_story_cards.title: Pet-Sitting Turned Into Running My Cousin's Free Hotel
recent_story_cards.twist: A shared calendar on the cousin's fridge reveals color-coded guest bookings for nearly every weekend, with the narrator listed as 'cat coverage' whenever paying for a sitter would have interfered.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The store blames user error and refuses an exchange after multiple incidents.
recent_story_cards.payoff: Your phone isn't panicking. Your case is.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman thinks her new phone is defective because emergency shortcuts activate randomly.
recent_story_cards.title: My Phone Kept Calling for Help by Itself
recent_story_cards.twist: A trendy third-party case has a slightly raised inner ridge pressing the side buttons whenever the phone flexes in a tight pocket.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The building says the plate is registered to her unit and threatens to suspend her access.
recent_story_cards.payoff: That plate was never your car.
recent_story_cards.premise: A tenant starts getting overnight parking fees for an unfamiliar car.
recent_story_cards.title: The Garage Charged Me for a Car I Don't Own
recent_story_cards.twist: A cleaner has been borrowing abandoned visitor tags and attaching them to staff cars to avoid overnight fees.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The list updates after every family dinner, making her wonder who he is shopping for.
recent_story_cards.payoff: It's not a second household. It's my brother getting back on his feet.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman sees a second weekly grocery list full of foods neither of them eats.
recent_story_cards.title: I Found My Boyfriend's Second Grocery List
recent_story_cards.twist: He has been quietly stocking a pantry for his recently divorced brother, who is embarrassed to admit money is tight.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The excuses become increasingly strange, and mutual friends seem to know something she doesn't.
recent_story_cards.payoff: I wasn't avoiding you. I was learning how to show up.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman suspects her best friend is avoiding her after repeated last-minute cancellations.
recent_story_cards.title: She Cancelled Every Dinner at the Last Minute
recent_story_cards.twist: Her friend has been secretly attending driving lessons after years of anxiety so she can drive the narrator to an important appointment when no one else is available.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The package shows delivered, the roommate acts suspicious, and friends are already posting spoilers.
recent_story_cards.payoff: I didn't steal launch day. I saved it.
recent_story_cards.premise: A gamer thinks his roommate stole a newly released game he had been waiting months to play.
recent_story_cards.title: My Roommate Stole My Game on Launch Day
recent_story_cards.twist: The roommate hid it because he organized a spoiler-free launch-night setup with food, blackout curtains, and their old gaming group joining remotely.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Nothing is stolen, but the movement happens repeatedly and her camera misses the exact moment.
recent_story_cards.payoff: Your chair gave me ten quiet minutes with him every day.
recent_story_cards.premise: A homeowner becomes obsessed with a porch chair that changes position while she is at work.
recent_story_cards.title: Someone Moved My Porch Chair Every Afternoon
recent_story_cards.twist: A schoolboy moves it each afternoon so his elderly grandfather can sit in the shade while waiting for him, then carefully returns it almost to the same spot.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The report contains risky recommendations, and leadership expects him to defend them in a client meeting.
recent_story_cards.payoff: The best part of this report belongs to her.
recent_story_cards.premise: An employee is praised for a polished report under his name that he did not create.
recent_story_cards.title: My Name Was on a Report I Never Wrote
recent_story_cards.twist: A junior analyst used his abandoned draft template to secretly build a proposal after being told she was too inexperienced to present ideas.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Her loyalty account shows three refunds and the manager says future returns may be blocked.
recent_story_cards.payoff: Those weren't your returns. Someone borrowed your purchase history.
recent_story_cards.premise: A customer is flagged for repeated returns she never made.
recent_story_cards.title: The Store Said I Returned Three Blenders
recent_story_cards.twist: A cashier has been attaching anonymous cash returns to active loyalty accounts to make suspicious no-receipt refunds look legitimate.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Other staff think he is secretly recording them, and a customer complains after noticing the glasses.
recent_story_cards.payoff: I'm not recording people. I'm trying to keep doing my job.
recent_story_cards.premise: A retail worker becomes suspicious when a coworker using new smart glasses seems to know inventory locations instantly.
recent_story_cards.title: His Smart Glasses Knew Where Everything Was
recent_story_cards.twist: He is testing an approved visual inventory assistant for accessibility because a recent hand injury makes using the handheld scanner painful.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Staff threaten to cancel his membership and charge a penalty.
recent_story_cards.payoff: You weren't sharing anything. Our gate was copying you.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man is accused of sharing his gym membership because his account logs two entries each morning.
recent_story_cards.title: The Gym Said I Was Sharing My Membership
recent_story_cards.twist: A faulty side-gate scanner has been replaying his successful tap whenever the maintenance worker tests the gate minutes later.

recent_story_cards.conflict: The hotel system shows a signed early-checkout request and staff initially refuse to restore the room.
recent_story_cards.payoff: We checked out the wrong person.
recent_story_cards.premise: A traveler returns from sightseeing to find his room deactivated and luggage moved.
recent_story_cards.title: The Hotel Checked Me Out While I Was Sightseeing
recent_story_cards.twist: Another guest with the same surname and first initial was checked out by a rushed desk clerk, and the signature belongs to that guest.

recent_story_cards.conflict: He refuses to show her the camera and keeps changing the subject before her mother's birthday.
recent_story_cards.payoff: I didn't sell our memories. I rescued them.
recent_story_cards.premise: A daughter thinks her father secretly sold a sentimental family camera.
recent_story_cards.title: Dad Said Our Old Camera Was Gone
recent_story_cards.twist: He sent it for restoration and digitization because it contains undeveloped photos from her parents' first trip together.

recent_story_cards.conflict: His match references conversations he never had, then another woman arrives at the same cafe expecting to meet him based on messages sent from his account.
recent_story_cards.payoff: Your practice dates are waiting for you.
recent_story_cards.premise: A man preparing for a first date realizes his roommate has been secretly using his dating profile to test pickup lines and has arranged a second date for the same evening.
recent_story_cards.title: My Roommate Accidentally Booked Me Two Dates
recent_story_cards.twist: The roommate admits he used the profile as a 'practice account' because he was too nervous to make his own, accidentally scheduling two real meetings.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Her party starts in an hour, the bakery insists the design matches the submitted form, and the cake says things like 'Q3 Synergy Champion' instead of Happy Birthday.
recent_story_cards.payoff: At least somebody finally achieved synergy.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman orders a custom birthday cake and receives one covered in bizarre corporate slogans because two bakery orders with nearly identical names were swapped.
recent_story_cards.title: The Bakery Sent Me a Corporate Awards Cake
recent_story_cards.twist: A panicked office manager arrives carrying the narrator's pastel birthday cake, which has just been unveiled at a serious quarterly awards meeting.

recent_story_cards.conflict: Cars keep appearing in her reserved space and the neighbor insists each driver is a visiting cousin, while building security threatens to fine her unit.
recent_story_cards.payoff: You built a parking business out of other people's spaces.
recent_story_cards.premise: A woman lends her parking space to a neighbor for one weekend, then discovers he has been selling weekday access to commuters while she is at work.
recent_story_cards.title: My Neighbor Rented Out My Parking Space
recent_story_cards.twist: A commuter shows her a recurring payment receipt for 'weekday reserved parking' with her exact bay number and the neighbor's payment handle.
